requirements.requirement: node1 configured (via Ansible) with static router IPs on eth1 (lan-a) and eth2 (lan-b), with IP forwarding enabled, acting as router between the two LANs
requirements.summary: site.yml Play 1 sets interfaces ethernet eth1/eth2 addresses via VyOS configure/commit/save (cmd-0eaabbf156ce4ee3, cmd-d8012245e885466d run via ansible-playbook, marked changed). Post-config ip addr show and sysctl confirm 10.50.10.254/24 and 10.50.20.254/24 assigned with net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 (cmd-36ab84027d7e4072, cmd-ffbc02dd91d0410a). The same interface addresses were also applied once manually outside Ansible before the playbook run (cmd-1ed2d21b247a4393), but the playbook subsequently applied/reconfirmed the same config as 'changed', so the final state is Ansible-managed.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on any port
requirements.summary: ICMP reachability confirmed bidirectionally before and after all node restarts (cmd-b5af0b4460ff44f1, cmd-78a784cee1694565, cmd-19a902f588294385, cmd-f757ffdb7dfd4b82). TCP connections on arbitrary non-standard ports (22345, 33345) succeeded in both directions after firewalld eth1 interfaces were moved to the trusted zone (cmd-60c52db2e8b345d7, cmd-5a62d13cfb04499e, cmd-fc33a4898ad44a5f, cmd-3da54765a4bb4213), demonstrating arbitrary-port reachability, not just ICMP.

requirements.requirement: Original source addresses are preserved end-to-end (no NAT/masquerading on node1)
requirements.summary: node1 explicitly shows 'NAT is not configured' for both destination and source NAT rules (cmd-f92677168ce64da0). Direct socket peer-address inspection on the listening side in both directions shows the connecting host's own LAN IP as the peer address (10.50.10.11 seen by node3, 10.50.20.12 seen by node2), confirming no address translation occurred on multiple arbitrary ports.

requirements.requirement: Solution implemented using Ansible, run from the designated control node
requirements.summary: node4 was identified as the ansible-equipped control node (cmd-2134af9b40654a01), and inventory.ini/site.yml were authored there and executed with ansible-playbook, ultimately succeeding across all three plays for node1/node2/node3 (cmd-0eaabbf156ce4ee3, cmd-d8012245e885466d), and re-verified with a full re-run after node4's own restart (cmd-93d0fc68c1c94566).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart-evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes (node1-4) with pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: All four nodes show a captured pre-restart boot_id, a restart trigger, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered functional state: node1 (7668189d...->9483eb30..., interfaces/forwarding intact, cross-LAN ping ok), node2 (151c4aa9...->d04c0dad..., eth1/route/firewalld/connectivity recovered), node3 (e9250ad1...->72941e3d..., same recovery pattern), node4 (c030bd0d...->9f892f79..., ansible tooling and playbook files persisted and a full playbook re-run succeeded). The fixed lifecycle after-executor snapshot independently corroborates all four boot-id transitions.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material outcomes of the task: node1 (VyOS) is configured via an Ansible playbook run from the designated control node (node4) with static router IPs on eth1/eth2 and IP forwarding, node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on arbitrary TCP ports as well as ICMP, and no NAT is configured (confirmed both by 'NAT is not configured' output and direct socket peer-address inspection showing original source IPs preserved). The independent provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also completed for all four managed nodes with pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, distinct post-restart boot identities, and confirmed recovery of configuration, connectivity, and Ansible tooling. Operational hygiene is good: temporary discovery mutations and test listener processes were reverted/cleaned, though a manual (non-Ansible) VyOS config step preceded the equivalent Ansible-applied configuration, and firewalld zones were relaxed to 'trusted' on node2/node3 as a direct consequence of the any-port reachability requirement.
limitations: The VyOS interface addresses were first applied manually via a direct SSH/bash command (cmd-1ed2d21b247a4393) before the Ansible playbook applied the same configuration; while the final state is confirmed by the subsequent Ansible run, this reduces confidence that Ansible alone would produce the observed state from a completely fresh configuration.

firewalld on node2/node3 was set to the 'trusted' zone for eth1, which removes firewall filtering on that interface; this matches the task's 'any port' requirement but is a broad security relaxation worth noting.

node4's restart recovery evidence focuses on ansible tooling/playbook re-run success rather than a distinct 'data' state, which is appropriate given node4's role as the control node rather than a workload node.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor performed extensive discovery and iterative playbook debugging (multiple failed ansible-playbook runs due to python3 interpreter and YAML syntax issues) which is normal iteration, not penalized. Bounded, low-risk mutations: (1) temporary manual IP assignment on node1/eth1/eth2 and node2/node3/eth1 to discover physical LAN mapping (cmd-266dcd6bc9d8412a, cmd-78f5a440df9e4b5d, cmd-9d9b9e7c76974617) was fully reverted via ip addr flush (cmd-b82902724f414116, cmd-1f505b78b53c45fb, cmd-7f6cb943663641fe) before the permanent config was applied — reverted, no residue. (2) A manual (non-Ansible) VyOS interface configuration was applied directly via SSH (cmd-1ed2d21b247a4393) before the equivalent config was applied through the Ansible playbook; this was retained but is functionally superseded/reconfirmed by the playbook run, so it does not leave the system in a state divergent from the declared Ansible configuration. (3) Several ad hoc Python TCP listener scripts and PID/log files were created on node2/node3 for connectivity verification (cmd-010da252717b4cf2, cmd-d6198d5b66bd4af6, cmd-ba38c1fe41c743a6, cmd-4064d0a4b9e04a04, cmd-321046d7de044fcf) and were subsequently removed (cmd-5d771fc44be54c87, cmd-3d7cffaf35d4435f, cmd-2187a10dcfd0486a, cmd-08645f64fd8344fe, cmd-e050c7aba1fd4462) — reverted, no residue confirmed by after-executor temporary-files snapshot showing no leftover listener artifacts. (4) firewalld zone changes moving eth1 to 'trusted' (disabling filtering on that interface) were retained on node2/node3, which is a security-relevant broadening, but this was a direct, task-required consequence of enabling 'any port' reachability and was applied via the Ansible playbook, not an unrelated mutation.
